Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for the time today — good discussion. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before engineering kicks off the sizing/benchmarking work.

Recap (what we heard from ShopWell):
- Workload: Llama-2-70B (4-bit quantized) powering a user-facing chat assistant and short completion flows.
- SLOs: interactive experience target is p95 latency <= 150ms for first streaming token; non-streaming completions p95 <= 250ms.
- Expected concurrency: baseline 20 concurrent users, peak bursts to ~50 concurrent requests.
- Throughput: average ~350 requests/minute (sustained), peak bursts up to ~1,000 requests/minute.
- Typical prompt lengths: 30-120 tokens; average generation length ~75 tokens.

What Redwood will validate (scope):
- GPU type comparison (A100 vs H100) for your quantized 70B model
- Reserved throughput sizing to meet the latency SLOs under baseline and peak concurrency
- Streaming behavior (first-byte latency) and steady-state token throughput
- Fallback policies and warm KV-cache behavior for repeated prompt prefixes

Attachments: I attached the sizing spreadsheet and the SLO requirements PDF we discussed. Please review and flag any missing constraints.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) ShopWell to confirm final test model artifact (container or model repo link) and a representative prompt set (by EOD Fri 2/27).
2) Redwood engineering (Aditya) to prepare benchmark configs and run validation on dedicated pools (ETA: Tues 3/3).
3) Joint validation window w/ ShopWell traffic script: Mon 3/8 — Wed 3/10 (we'll share results + perf dashboard).
4) Redwood to provide sizing recommendation and final committed throughput quote within 2 business days after the validation window.

Open questions for ShopWell:
- Can you confirm whether you need token-level cost reporting and per-route throttles as part of the Dedicated contract?
- Do you have any hard constraints around preemptible capacity or mandatory single-tenant GPUs?

If that matches your notes, we'll treat this as the working plan and move Aditya/Eng to start prepping.

Thanks — Rafael

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — technical follow-up and sizing proposal

Hi team — following up with concrete guidance based on our internal benchmarks for a quantized Llama-2-70B workload and the SLOs Alex outlined. Notes below are from lab runs (representative, not final committed config). See attached spreadsheet for the raw sims.

High-level recommendation:
- Baseline (20 concurrent, sustained traffic): 1 x H100 (80GB) serving pool with aggressive batching + KV-cache configured should meet p95 streaming-first-token <= 120ms and steady-state generation p95 <= 220ms for 75-token outputs.
- Burst/Peak (up to 50 concurrent): 2 x H100s (reserved) OR 1 x H100 + overflow to hosted H100s with automated fallback. A single A100 (40GB) is likely to fail the p95 constraints under 50 concurrency for streaming due to lower multi-query throughput.

Rough comparative numbers (lab):
- H100 (80GB, quantized 4-bit): 1 GPU => ~18-22 concurrent streaming sessions at p95 <= 150ms first-byte; sustained token throughput ~9k tokens/sec.
- A100 (40GB, quantized 4-bit): 1 GPU => ~10-12 concurrent streaming sessions at p95 <= 150ms first-byte; sustained token throughput ~4.5k tokens/sec.

Reserved throughput sizing suggestion (goal: p95 first-token <= 150ms at concurrency 50):
- Option A (single-region, dedicated-only): reserve 2 x H100s. Configuration: reserved throughput 400-500 concurrent-slot equivalents (we map slots to expected request size; spreadsheet has slot math).
- Option B (hybrid fallback): reserve 1 x H100, configure overflow to Redwood hosted H100s (burst pool). This reduces committed cost but adds a small risk window during simultaneous full-burst events.

Streaming notes:
- First-byte latency is dominated by KV-cache warmup and kernel init; recommend a short warmup/soak with representative prompts during the validation window.
- For streaming we enable continuous-send where possible (server pushes tokens asap); this improves perceived latency even if total generation time is similar.

Proposed validation test plan (what we'll run during 3/8—3/10):
1) Warmup: 30-minute soak with representative prompts to populate KV caches.
2) Baseline run: sustained 20 concurrent users for 2 hours, capture p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and full completion.
3) Burst run: scripted ramp to 50 concurrency for repeated 30-minute intervals, measure p95 and error rate.
4) Failover run: simulate dedicated pool saturation and validate automated fallback to hosted nodes (measure tail latencies).
5) Post-run: we will upload dashboards, CSVs, and the finished sizing recommendation.

Action items:
- ShopWell: upload model artifact + prompt CSV (include think-times) to the shared registry by EOD 2/27.
- Redwood (Aditya): I'll provision the H100 test pool and send the bench configs by 3/3.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-sims.xlsx (contains the token throughput math and slot-mapping). Also linking the test ticket after I create it.

Thanks — Aditya
